title: Hot Cocoa Mix

adjustment.analysis: No known drivers for the target week: no events, no price change, no promotion. The classical uplift model's 0.60 multiplier reflects a 'week after promotion' effect, but the last promotion was on 2026-06-15 (Father's Day), which was already a low-sales holiday week (x0.22). That week was not a typical promotion, and its follow-up week (2026-06-22) is not a repeat of a standard post-promo dip. The noise-adjusted post-promo effect is x0.6, but evidence is weak and contextually mismatched. No other drivers exist. The baseline median is 7.9, and recent weeks show low volume. No justification to adjust below baseline. The model's 0.60 is overcorrecting.

brief:

TARGET WEEK: 2026-06-22 to 2026-06-28 (next week)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:

  shelf price: 5.03 (+0.0% vs regular price 5.03)

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 7.9 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 21.3 | 10%-90%: 0.0 - 20.3

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-54% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
